references.text: The parallel account in Numbers describes how the spies traveled through the land from the Wilderness of Sin to Rehob and came to the Valley of Eshkol, where they cut off a cluster of grapes.
Specifically mentions the Valley of Eshkol (נַחַל אֶשְׁכֹּל) where the spies cut off a cluster of grapes, which explains the meaning of the name.
Refers to the Valley of Eshkol in connection with the spies' mission and how they viewed the land.
Joshua sends spies to explore the land, especially Jericho, in a similar way that Moses sent spies to explore Canaan.
The book of Hebrews refers to those who came out of Egypt under Moses and their disobedience, which included events related to the spies' mission.
